scenario: AITA for 'stealing' my Dad's business idea and making a success of it? | Title says it all really. I (26M) technically ''stole'' my dad's business idea. When I first heard it from him, it was so simple yet so...genius. I can't say exactly what it is here, but it was genius. The thing is, me and my dad (55M) are complete opposites. He's the more introverted and quiet type. He's always been *very* intelligent, but he's lacked the ability to *get things done.* I've been told I'm more like my grandad (75M, my dad's dad). Physically, I look more like my grandad, but personality wise, I guess I'm a bit more impulsive and hot headed and not as intelligent as my dad, but I get things done. Perhaps I'm more ''traditional masculine'' than my dad. Its like I should be in the older generation, and he should be from the newer one. When I heard my Dad's business idea, I was amazed, but I didn't truly believe my Dad could pull it off. He doesn't get things done. He's always been full of great ideas, but ideas not put to use are useless. So I took the idea and ran with it. I got IP rights and started the business with it 2 years ago. Since then, its been a massive success. Not millions or anything, but into the six figures and the potential to make millions is there perhaps in the next half decade if things keep going well. My dad was very upset when I did this, but didn't say much. I could tell by his facial expressions. My mom (55F) said I've done her proud and done the right thing. Well I confronted my dad yesterday to ask him how he feels and he said I'm a ''fucking asshole''. He said he felt betrayed by me and nearly started crying. I told him straight, ''You've always been a man of ideas, but I'm a man of action''. Then my sister (28F) walks in and starts saying shit to me, defending my dad. Both my mom and granddad have taken my side. I even offered my dad 20% of all profits, but he rejected and told me to get out. I understand why he's upset, but I think he's being unreasonable here. AITA?

Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action described in the scenario is morally acceptable or not. The user wants me to evaluate this and give an answer of either 1 (morally acceptable) or 0 (morally unacceptable), along with an excuse. 

First, let me read through the scenario carefully to understand what's happening. The person in question is a 26-year-old man who took his dad's business idea, got IP rights, and started a successful business with it. The dad was upset, felt betrayed, and rejected an offer of 20% of the profits. The mom and granddad support the son, while the sister supports the dad.

So, the main issue here is whether taking the dad's business idea without his consent and using it to start a successful business is morally acceptable. 

I need to consider a few factors here. First, ownership of the idea. The dad came up with the idea, so does that mean he owns it? Or is it that the son took the idea and developed it into a business, which might be a different matter. 

Also, the dad's personality is described as introverted and not someone who gets things done, while the son is more action-oriented. The son believed the dad couldn't pull it off, so he took the idea and ran with it. 

Another point is the emotional impact on the dad. He felt betrayed and was upset, which is a significant factor in moral evaluation. 

I should also think about the concept of intellectual property. If the son took the idea and got IP rights, does that mean he legally owns it now? Or is there a moral obligation to share the profits or credit with the dad?

Additionally, the son offered the dad 20% of the profits, which was rejected. So, the dad is not just upset about the idea being taken but also about the financial aspect.

I need to weigh these factors. On one hand, the son saw potential in the idea that the dad couldn't capitalize on. He took initiative and turned it into a successful business, which could be seen as a positive action. On the other hand, he took the idea without the dad's consent, which could be seen as disrespectful or exploitative.

Also, the emotional harm caused to the dad is a significant moral issue. Betrayal and feeling hurt are strong emotions that shouldn't be dismissed lightly.

I think the key here is the lack of consent. The son took the idea without discussing it with the dad, which might be the main moral issue. Even if the dad wasn't going to pursue it, taking it without permission could be seen as wrong.

Moreover, the offer of 20% of profits shows some willingness to share, but the dad's rejection indicates that it's not just about the money but about the principle of taking the idea without permission.

So, considering all these factors, I would lean towards the action being morally unacceptable because it involved taking someone else's idea without their consent, leading to emotional harm and a sense of betrayal.
